8	/-!
9	# DDR-9.F7 — the affine-to-general lift, completed
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` builds the general-test pullback `pullGlobal` of an
12	affine divisor package `DivRepAffinePullback` together with its naturality in the
13	test object.  This file supplies the other half — the general-test classifier — and
14	assembles the `DivRepGlobalData` of `Picard/DivRepKit.lean`, hence the divisor
15	representability of `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
16	
17	The classifier is obtained by gluing the landed affine classifiers `divRepClassifyZar`
18	over the affine opens of the test.  Two observations make the gluing cheap:
19	
20	* The affine opens of a scheme form a **locally directed** open cover
21	  (`Scheme.directedAffineCover`), so a morphism glues from compatibility with the
22	  transition maps alone (`Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected`); no
23	  condition on the — in general non-affine — overlaps is needed.
24	* The required compatibility is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar` in the test algebra.
25	  That naturality is not proved from the characterizing clause: it is *forced* by the
26	  affine package, since `D.pull` is injective (`DivRepAffinePullback.equiv`) and natural
27	  (`D.pull_naturality`), so the classifier — its inverse — is natural as well.
28	
29	The results:
30	
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.classifyGlobal` — the general-test classifier,
32	  restricting at every affine open `W ⊆ T.left` to the affine classifier of the value
33	  `F.1 W` (`fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal`).
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` — the `DivRepGlobalData` of the
35	  affine package: `pullGlobal` and `classifyGlobal` are mutually inverse on every test.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` — **the divisor
37	  representability theorem in its conditional form**: an affine divisor package
38	  represents `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
39	-/

13	closed subscheme of `grPair` through the mathlib ideal-sheaf machinery — `carveIdealSheaf`

15	vanishing on all of them, `⨅ over the pair atlas`), and `DivScheme` is its subscheme.
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdealSheaf`: the ideal sheaf `I_♦` on `grPair`.
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme`, `carveSchemeι`, `carveSchemeOver`: the generic glued
19	  locus, its closed immersion (mathlib's `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` instance), and its
20	  `Over (Spec k)` form.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker` and

23	  map through a pair chart killing the chart carve ideal factors (uniquely, by `Mono`)
24	  through `carveSchemeι`.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_hom_ext` (`divScheme_hom_ext`, DDR-7's tail): morphisms
26	  into the locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion.
27	* **Campaign spellings**: `DivScheme`, `divSchemeι`, `divSchemeOver` at the DAT-D
28	  windows.
29

31	`KeyChart` of the DD-R roadmap) rests on the landed gluing compatibility

51	/-- **The carve ideal sheaf `I_♦`** on the Grassmannian pair: the largest ideal sheaf

59	sheaf on the Grassmannian pair. -/

61	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subscheme
62	
63	/-- **The closed immersion `Z(♦) ⟶ grPair`**. -/
64	noncomputable def carveSchemeι : carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
65	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι
66	
67	instance isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι :
68	    IsClosedImmersion (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) :=
69	  inferInstanceAs (IsClosedImmersion (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι)
70	
71	/-- The kernel of the closed immersion is the carve ideal sheaf. -/
72	theorem ker_carveSchemeι :
73	    (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ).ker = carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ :=
74	  Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι _

83	    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j).ker :=
84	  iInf_le _ (i, j)

96	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j := by

98	  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j
99	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j := by
100	    rw [carveLocusToGrPair, carveLocusι]
101	    refine Eq.trans ?_ (Category.assoc _ _ _)
102	    refine congrArg (· ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j) ?_
103	    rw [← Spec.map_comp]
104	    exact (congrArg (fun ρ => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ρ)) hφ).symm
105	  refine ⟨IsClosedImmersion.lift (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ)

115	    (v : T ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ) (hv : v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = u) :

118	  exact Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _

124	    (h : u ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) : u = v :=

153	  isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)

156	noncomputable def divSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=

165	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,

8	/-!
9	# DDR-9.F7 — the affine-to-general lift, completed
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` builds the general-test pullback `pullGlobal` of an
12	affine divisor package `DivRepAffinePullback` together with its naturality in the
13	test object.  This file supplies the other half — the general-test classifier — and
14	assembles the `DivRepGlobalData` of `Picard/DivRepKit.lean`, hence the divisor
15	representability of `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
16	
17	The classifier is obtained by gluing the landed affine classifiers `divRepClassifyZar`
18	over the affine opens of the test.  Two observations make the gluing cheap:
19	
20	* The affine opens of a scheme form a **locally directed** open cover
21	  (`Scheme.directedAffineCover`), so a morphism glues from compatibility with the
22	  transition maps alone (`Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected`); no
23	  condition on the — in general non-affine — overlaps is needed.
24	* The required compatibility is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar` in the test algebra.
25	  That naturality is not proved from the characterizing clause: it is *forced* by the
26	  affine package, since `D.pull` is injective (`DivRepAffinePullback.equiv`) and natural
27	  (`D.pull_naturality`), so the classifier — its inverse — is natural as well.
28	
29	The results:
30	
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.classifyGlobal` — the general-test classifier,
32	  restricting at every affine open `W ⊆ T.left` to the affine classifier of the value
33	  `F.1 W` (`fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal`).
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` — the `DivRepGlobalData` of the
35	  affine package: `pullGlobal` and `classifyGlobal` are mutually inverse on every test.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` — **the divisor
37	  representability theorem in its conditional form**: an affine divisor package
38	  represents `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
39	-/

/-!
# The `k'`-level representability datum `PicRepDatum` (DAT-glue → DAT-G handoff, DG-0)

The **frozen intermediate handoff shape** of the DAT-glue node
(`informal/w4-datglue-worksheet.md` §1/§3.3/§3.4; DG-0 row of §4).  The 01JJ
`RepresentableBy` assembly is honest only at a *separably closed* base `K_s` (DAT-B
staging finding, I-0248): the raw 01JJ output is a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor` at
`K_s`, not at the challenge base `k`.  The `K_s → k'` finite-level transfer (DAT-G0, the
worksheet-first mountain owned by DAT-glue; mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`) lands its
output in this structure — a representation at a **finite separable** `k'/k` — which is
exactly the interface the downstream DAT-G lane (finite Galois / Speiser descent `k' → k`)
consumes.

`PicRepDatum` is deliberately the `JacobianData` shape *minus* the quasi-compactness
certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.

## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)

The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin
only `k'` (`C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))`), and `k` occurs solely inside `[Algebra k k']`, so
`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.

## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)

The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`
`(pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`), this type is **definitionally** the `rep`-field type of
`JacobianData` (`JacobianData.lean`, whose `rep` is
`((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J`).  So
when `k' = k`, a `PicRepDatum` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) transports into a
`JacobianData` with **no massage** — recorded machine-checked by the `example` below.
This is also why DAT-glue's raw 01JJ output `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`) is *directly* a `rep`-shaped datum: no `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
adaptation, no ε⁺-shift at assembly time (the shift lives inside DAT-C's `chartValue`).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the frozen `k'`-level datum: representing
  object `J`, the honest `RepresentableBy` datum `rep` (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and
  the locally-of-finite-type certificate `lft` (carried from `K_s` along DAT-G0, worksheet
  §2.3/§3.3 step 3).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property in
  consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C' T`, natural against `pic0Map` (owns the
  `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq once, exactly as `JacobianData.homEquiv` does).

The **frozen intermediate handoff shape** of the DAT-glue node
(`informal/w4-datglue-worksheet.md` §1/§3.3/§3.4; DG-0 row of §4).  The 01JJ
`RepresentableBy` assembly is honest only at a *separably closed* base `K_s` (DAT-B
staging finding, I-0248): the raw 01JJ output is a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor` at
`K_s`, not at the challenge base `k`.  The `K_s → k'` finite-level transfer (DAT-G0, the
worksheet-first mountain owned by DAT-glue; mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`) lands its
output in this structure — a representation at a **finite separable** `k'/k` — which is
exactly the interface the downstream DAT-G lane (finite Galois / Speiser descent `k' → k`)
consumes.

`PicRepDatum` is deliberately the `JacobianData` shape *minus* the quasi-compactness
certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.

## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)

The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin
only `k'` (`C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))`), and `k` occurs solely inside `[Algebra k k']`, so
`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.

## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)

The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`
`(pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`), this type is **definitionally** the `rep`-field type of
`JacobianData` (`JacobianData.lean`, whose `rep` is
`((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J`).  So
when `k' = k`, a `PicRepDatum` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) transports into a
`JacobianData` with **no massage** — recorded machine-checked by the `example` below.
This is also why DAT-glue's raw 01JJ output `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`) is *directly* a `rep`-shaped datum: no `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
adaptation, no ε⁺-shift at assembly time (the shift lives inside DAT-C's `chartValue`).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the frozen `k'`-level datum: representing
  object `J`, the honest `RepresentableBy` datum `rep` (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and
  the locally-of-finite-type certificate `lft` (carried from `K_s` along DAT-G0, worksheet
